## What's Changed
- Fix: agent prompts no longer silently disable Code Review Graph under V2 Code Mode (#167). The six CRG-enabled agent prompts now use the two-signal detection rule (delegation note or `code-review-graph_*` tools in the native list or the Code Mode catalog inside `execute`), docs/CONFIGURATION.md gains the "Code Review Graph (CRG) under V2 Code Mode" setup section, and the profiler's CRG reference is fixed.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/NicoGenti/opencode-orchestrator-kit/compare/v1.2.0...v1.2.1

## Highlights

- Include the canonical project README in the npm package as a generated `plugin/README.md`.
- Add comprehension-coach evidence modes and actionable `NEEDS_REVIEW` recovery guidance (#137, #141).
- Add path-traversal guards to Python helper scripts (#128–#135).
- Add deterministic context-budget and evidence-check gates (#151).
- Document cache configuration, session reuse, and cache-aware prompt design (#119, #120).
- Add optional, read-only Code Review Graph support for implementation, test selection, and planning, with seven benchmark metrics (#153).

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and `bun run sync-assets --check` passed.
- `bun test`: 1,200 passed, 30 failed. The clean baseline had 1,197 passed and 31 failed; the release failure set is a subset, with no release-only failures.
- `bun run format:check` reported 120 warnings versus 121 on the clean baseline; the release set is a subset.
- The npm package contains 46 files, and its README matches the root README byte-for-byte.
- Code review approved with no blocking findings.

The release workflow is configured to publish to npm on pushed `v*` tags; check its run for publication status.

### Changed

- **`TIER_FAST` moves to `ollama/mimo-v2.6-flash:cloud`**: every agent on the fast tier (`profiler`, `explorer`, `librarian`, `build-helper`, `npm-helper`, `deploy-helper`, `comprehension-coach`, and the opt-in `pc-doctor` and `writer` extras) now resolves to `mimo-v2.6-flash:cloud` instead of `minimax-m3.1-flash:cloud`. `plugin/src/tiers.ts`, `templates/models.config.json` and the pin in `tests/ollama-preset.test.ts` move together; the test now accepts both `:<size>cloud` and `-cloud` model suffixes. No agent, command, skill or contract changes, so this is a patch.

### Added

- **`orchestrator-quick`**: a second `mode: primary` agent (3,596-character prompt against the orchestrator's 23,961) for small tasks. Same read-only surface and the same kit invariants — it cannot edit application code, run the plan board or write `.context` — but its cycle is one classify, one delegation and one verification, with an explicit hand-back to `orchestrator` when the task needs more than one delegation, more than about five files, or must survive the session. `plugin/src/permissions.ts` now treats both routers through a `ROUTING_AGENTS` set instead of a hardcoded `"orchestrator"` in three places.
- **`/quick`**: packaged command that switches the session to `orchestrator-quick` and states the working rules (one delegation, raw verification output, stop and escalate when the task grows). Five commands are registered at runtime.
- **Small-task triage**: `agents/orchestrator.md` tells the full router to hand a one-file or plan-free request to `/quick` instead of running the multi-agent flow, citing the measured 2-3x cost.

### Changed

- **English-only shipped text**: the Italian prose left in `command/recall.md`, `agents/{profiler,comprehension-coach}.md`, `templates/design-rules.md`, `templates/models.config.json`, `docs/*.md` and in the comments/messages of `scripts/` and `plugin/src/` is now English. `scripts/plan-board.py` and `plugin/src/plan-board.ts` carry the same translated messages, so the parity test still compares like with like. Test titles and comments are untouched: renaming them touches `tests/fixtures/baseline-failures.txt` and belongs to its own change.
- **Agent descriptions compressed**: the 18 frontmatter `description:` fields now carry one role sentence plus an explicit `Not for …` scope where two agents compete (build/npm/deploy helpers, code-reviewer/security, profiler/librarian, developer-fixer/test-engineer). Total 3.178 characters, down from 3.830; `tests/agent-descriptions.test.ts` caps each description at 260 characters and pins the routing terms that must survive a future edit.
- **Orchestrator prompt trimmed to 22.652 characters** (was 23.961, against a 24.000 cap — 39 characters of headroom left): the six subsections `Context slicing` … `Research mode` no longer restate what `skills/comprehension-workflow/SKILL.md` and `command/{recall,research-mode}.md` already define as canonical; every contract sentence asserted by `tests/recall-command.test.ts`, `tests/telemetry-writer.test.ts` and `tests/comprehension-config.test.ts` is preserved verbatim. The budget guard W1 now covers all 18 agent prompts at current size + 5%, so a prompt can shrink freely and can only grow by editing the table on purpose.
- **`AGENTS.md` down to 11.617 characters** (was 15.552, −25%): the `Prompt-Assembly Stable-Prefix Contract` block — stable prefix, boundary baseline, frontmatter key order, single primary agent — moved verbatim to `CONTRIBUTING.md#prompt-assembly-stable-prefix-contract`, where contributors read it and no agent pays for it on every request. `AGENTS.md` keeps a four-line pointer; `tests/agents-instructions-budget.test.ts` caps the file at 12.000 characters and fails if the contract comes back.

### Removed

- **GitHub automation beyond CI**: `.github/workflows/agent-issue.yml` (comment `/agent` and label `agent:run`) went away with its runner prompt (`.github/agent/agent-issue.md`) and CI model preset (`.github/agent/ci-free.json`); so did the plan-board issue mirror — `.github/workflows/plan-adopt.yml`, `.github/workflows/plan-sync.yml`, `scripts/issue_bridge.py` and the `plan:*` labels. The repository now runs only `test.yml`, `deploy.yml` and `release.yml`: code arrives through a normal pull request, and the board in `plan/` is local to the repository. `tests/no-github-automation.test.ts` fails if that set changes, if a workflow triggers on `issues`/`issue_comment`, runs `opencode run`, calls `gh issue`, reads `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, or uses a `plan:*` label. ## opencode-orchestrator-kit v1.0.0

First stable release, and the first one published to npm.

bash
npm install opencode-orchestrator-kit


Add it to the plugins array in your opencode.json (options: preset, withExtras). The install.sh copy-based installer remains available for OpenCode v1.

### Highlights

- *npm distribution*: the plugin is now published as [opencode-orchestrator-kit](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-orchestrator-kit) with provenance. Releases are tag-driven (v*) and gated by tests, typecheck, lint, formatting, asset parity and a tag/version check.
- *Hardened agent permissions* for OpenCode v2 last-match-wins semantics: every agent has explicit shell, skill and subagent catch-alls; developer-fixer can no longer commit, push or merge, and asks before npx, dotnet, ng, docker build and skill scripts; destructive find flags are denied; only the orchestrator may spawn developer-fixer.
- *Accurate skill allowlists*: agents only allow skills that actually ship, plus two reserved prefixes: web-* for web-stack skill packs and project-* for a consuming project's own skills.
- *Companion kit contract*: a documented, optional extension contract so other skill kits can plug in without the kit depending on any of them.
- */close-session* is now registered by the plugin alongside /start-session, /recall and /research-mode.

### Tooling

- bun run bump-version <x.y.z> keeps both manifests and the changelog in sync.
- bun run sync-assets regenerates the packaged plugin/assets/ mirror (--check in CI).
- CI now runs typecheck, lint and format checks over source, tests and scripts.

### Fixes

- install.sh: --with-examples works, new --upgrade/--force with backups, extras install into agents/.
- Plan-board write protection now lives in each agent's own frontmatter.
- plan-writer prefers the native plan_board tool and accepts python3.
- The agent issue workflow uses the current checkout (or AGENT_KIT_SHA) and the AGENT_MODEL repository variable.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/NicoGenti/opencode-orchestrator-kit/blob/v1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md) for the full list.

*Full diff*: https://github.com/NicoGenti/opencode-orchestrator-kit/compare/v0.7.0...v1.0.0
